topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains how local treatments remove or destroy tumours and why their success depends on tumour accessibility and spread.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This section examines how broadly cell-damaging drugs treat cancer and how their effectiveness is constrained by toxicity and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains how blocking hormonal growth signals can control cancers that remain dependent on those signals.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how missing cell cycle checkpoint proteins create vulnerabilities that treatments can exploit selectively.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This section explains how inhibiting one DNA repair pathway selectively kills cancer cells already deficient in another.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the rationale for identifying oncogenic drivers and inhibiting the proteins on which tumour growth depends.

topics.label: Limitations and resistance in kinase inhibitor treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibition often becomes long-term disease management rather than a cure as cancer cells evade treatment.

topics.label: Antibody-directed cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognising cancer cell surface proteins direct therapeutic effects towards those cells.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This section evaluates whether the body's existing immune system protects against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and tumour recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade restores antitumour T cell activity and why tumour neoantigens influence its effectiveness.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells towards cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine treatments that deliberately equip or position T cells to recognise and attack tumour cells.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and personalised strategies
topics.groupedBecause: This section considers how treatment can be matched and adapted to patients despite cancer heterogeneity and resistance.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This section assesses improvements in cancer outcomes in light of changing incidence and the contributions of prevention and detection.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how to pursue better cancer treatment when clinical decisions and trials must balance prospective benefits against established outcomes and quality of life.
